issue.title: EQL: revising usage of quote (single or double) for escaping identifiers

labels.name: Team:QL (Deprecated)
labels.description: Meta label for query languages team

repository.name: elasticsearch
repository.description: Free and Open Source, Distributed, RESTful Search Engine

issue.body:
User feedback when running an EQL query: I cannot escape the event category for the query: `system.cpu where cpu.cores = 16`
```
line 1:8: mismatched input '.' expecting 'where'
```

Tried escaping (with " or \"):
` "system.cpu" where ...`
```
line 1:1: no viable alternative at input '\"system.cpu\"'"
```

Finally fixed by using backticks:
``` `system.cpu` where ...```

This is a poor experience from an internal uses, that is interested in EQL and know about it. And yet gets caught off-guard by our use of quotes and escaping.

I'm raising this issue to revisit this topic and improve the current situation.

issue.title: EQL: Fix syntax for event type

labels.name: Team:QL (Deprecated)
labels.description: Meta label for query languages team

repository.name: elasticsearch
repository.description: Free and Open Source, Distributed, RESTful Search Engine

issue.body:
Event type is actually a string value for `event.category` which can
contain any kind of characters, or start with a digit, which currently
is not supported, so we introduce the possibility to be able to use the
usual syntax of `"` and `"""` for strings and raw strings.

Make the grammar a bit cleaner by using the `identifier` only where it's
actually an identifier in terms of query scemantics.

Fixes: #62933

body:
(Looks like this comment never got submitted to GitHub. Posting it now.)

I'm not sure that I agree with the premise of the issue, I think if you look at EQL in Elasticsearch within a vacuum, then yes, the event type is purely an alias for `event.category == "<eventType>"`.

However, I don't think you can or should look at it in a vacuum. At the most basic level, an identifier is just a name for something. For EQL in Endgame, each event type actually had a separate schema. So if you did `process where X` then the condition X is validated against the `process` event schema. Also, for those implementations, the event type actually lives both outside and inside the event data. The event type is basically the name for the class of events you're looking at.

When we were first exploring EQL, we actually had a length discussion (https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/49462) about how the "event type" concept will translate into Elasticsearch. It wasn't an obvious choice and there were pros and cons for several possible approaches. That just emphasizes how choosing to use `event.category` as the matched field is purely an implementation detail and not a property of the language or specification itself.

Since the `event.category` alias is an implementation detail of EQL in Elasticsearch, then what should be the syntax that's captured in the grammar/specification? I think an identifier (since it's just a name anyway) actually makes sense. "I'm looking for `eventType` events that match `condition`". You're naming the type of event that you're looking for.  EQL has pipe identifiers, function name identifiers and field name identifiers. I'm not sure why the syntax for event type identifiers should be special and look like strings, instead of using the `` `<escaped event type>` `` notation, which already represents an escaped identifier that may contain special characters
